title: Boss: prove the signup page opens
brief:
No starter code, no comments to fill in. Write the test.

**The behaviour to prove:** from the home page, clicking **Signup / Login** opens the login page, and the **New User Signup!** form is there when it does.

A reviewer will expect:

- a test function named after the behaviour, not after the page
- the browser tab as the `page` argument
- an assertion on the address *and* one on what is on screen
- role-based locators where the element has a visible name

This is step 3 of `learn/test_tc01_register_user.py`, written from scratch.
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_signup_login_link_opens_the_signup_form(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    page.get_by_role("link", name="Signup / Login").click()

    expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/login")
    expect(page.get_by_text("New User Signup!")).to_be_visible()

checks.label: Your test reaches the login page
checks.feedback: The shop did not end up on /login. The menu link is labelled "Signup / Login" - spaces and slash included.

checks.label: You get there by clicking, not by navigating straight to the URL
checks.feedback: You went straight to /login with goto(). That tests the page, but not the LINK - and the link is the behaviour we are proving. Start at the home page and click.

checks.name: to_be_visible
checks.label: You assert the signup form is on screen
checks.feedback: Nothing checked that the form rendered. A URL can be right while the page behind it is empty - that is a real failure mode, and worth one more line.

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: Same shape as the last challenge: goto, click, two expects. The only new thing is that you write the def line yourself.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: def test_signup_login_link_opens_the_signup_form(page: Page): then goto the home page, click get_by_role("link", name="Signup / Login"), then assert the URL is .../login and that get_by_text("New User Signup!") is visible.

reveal:
Base Camp cleared.

You can now write a test that a reviewer would merge: named for its behaviour, arranged-acted-asserted in order, waiting properly, and reading like a sentence.

Next: **The Locator Forest**, where the interesting question stops being "what do I check" and becomes "how do I find it".
